source_caption:
Léon: The Professional (1994) gave Natalie Portman one of the most remarkable debut performances in movie history.

She was only 11 when she was cast as Mathilda, and had to audition multiple times after initially being considered too young. Portman eventually won the role after competing against thousands of actresses. 

What makes her performance so impressive is how naturally she balances Mathilda’s vulnerability, anger and confidence. This wasn’t just a child actor delivering lines — Portman gave the character a real emotional arc, and somehow held her own alongside Jean Reno and Gary Oldman in her very first film.

Behind the scenes, she even had to learn how to cry on cue. During one early emotional scene, she struggled to produce tears, so Luc Besson had a crew member use mint oil near her eyes. Portman later recalled that the experience taught her to cry on command very quickly. 

Portman has spoken warmly about the experience over the years. In 2025, she still described making Léon at 11 as a wonderful first experience, saying everyone treated her well and that working with Reno and Oldman inspired her. She also said the experience made acting feel like “playing” — something she still carries with her today.

It’s pretty incredible to watch Léon now knowing that this was Natalie Portman’s very first movie.

And somehow, she already looked like she belonged there.
